title: Part One, Chapter 6: The Fall of Vucub-caquix

verses.t: And here follows the account of the blowgun shot that the two boys gave Vucub-caquix, and how each of them was destroyed for his pride.

This Vucub-caquix had a tree, a nance tree, because this was his only food, and every day he climbed the nance tree to eat the fruit. Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque had seen that this was his food, and the two boys lay in wait beneath the tree, hidden among the leaves of the undergrowth. And then Vucub-caquix arrived, and when he had climbed up into the tree, Hun-ahpu shot him with a pellet that went straight and struck him on the jaw, and he fell to the ground screaming. And as soon as Hun-ahpu saw Vucub-caquix fall, he ran in great haste and stooped to seize him; but then Vucub-caquix seized Hun-ahpu's arm and tore it off at the end of the shoulder, and then Hun-ahpu let go of Vucub-caquix. And so the two boys came out of it well, because they were not defeated by Vucub-caquix. And he went off to his house carrying Hun-ahpu's arm and holding his jaw. "What has happened to you, sir?" said Chimalmat to her husband Vucub-caquix. "What should it be? Two demons shot me with a blowgun and knocked my jaw out of joint; all my teeth are loose and they hurt me badly. But here I have brought the arm of one of them; hang it over the fire in the smoke, so that the two demons will come for it," said Vucub-caquix. And then she hung up Hun-ahpu's arm. And then Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque discussed what they ought to do, and having discussed it, they went and told it to an old man whose head was already white, and to an old woman who was truly very old; and so great was the age of both that they already walked bent over. The old man was called Saquinimac, and the old woman was called Saquinima-tzitz (a great white coati). And the two boys said to the old man and the old woman, "Come with us to fetch our arm from the house of Vucub-caquix. We shall go behind you, as if we were your grandchildren whose father and mother have died. And so when they ask you, say that we go about behind you, and that you know how to take out the worm that eats the molars and the teeth. And so Vucub-caquix will see us only as boys, and we shall advise you." This is what the two boys said. "Very well," said the old people. And then they went to the corner of the house of Vucub-caquix, who was lying back on his throne; and the two old people passed by, with the two boys playing behind them, and they passed below the house of Vucub-caquix. And he was screaming with the pain of his tooth; and when Vucub-caquix saw the two old people and the boys, he asked them, "Where do you come from, grandparents?" "We go about looking for our living, lord," they said. "What do you do for a living? Are those your children who go with you?" "No, lord, they are our grandchildren; but we take pity on them, lord, and of whatever we find we give them a piece of tortilla," said the old people. And meanwhile the lord was suffering badly from his tooth and could only speak with great effort: "I beg you to take pity on me. What is it you do? What do you cure?" said the lord. "Lord, what we cure," said the old people, "is to take out the worm from the teeth and molars; and we cure eyes, and we also set broken bones." "Very well; if that is true, cure my teeth, for I have no rest and cannot sleep, and my eyes hurt me as well. This began when two demons shot me with a pellet, and so I cannot eat. So have mercy on me, for all my teeth are loose." "Very well, lord; it is a worm that is hurting you. We shall take out those teeth and put others in their place." "But perhaps that will not be good? For it is by them that I am a lord, and by my teeth and my eyes alone." And they said, "We shall put others in place of those; we shall put in ground bone." But this ground bone was only white maize. "Very well," said the lord, "take them out; help me." And then they took out the teeth of Vucub-caquix, and it was only white maize that they put in their place; and the kernels of maize gleamed in his mouth. And then his face fell, and he never looked like a lord again. They finished taking out all his teeth, and his mouth was left bruised. And when they cured the eyes of Vucub-caquix, they skinned the pupils of his eyes and took away all his silver, and he did not feel it; and with it taken out he was left staring, but he was no longer great and no longer proud. And this was done by the counsel of Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque. And Vucub-caquix died, and then Hun-ahpu took back his arm; and Chimalmat, the wife of Vucub-caquix, also died; and so the riches of Vucub-caquix were lost. And the healer took all the precious stones that had made him proud here on the earth. And the old man and the old woman who did this were gods. And when they took back the arm, they put it in its place, and it joined together again and was whole. And they wished to do this only to bring about the death of Vucub-caquix, because his pride seemed wrong to them. And afterwards the two boys went away again; and this was done so by the command of the Heart of the Sky.
